cases.title: First lesson: asks what should snap before proposing; candidates as questions, at most three; real names

rubric.reason: The mentor opens Turn 1 by explaining key types ('Today's idea: every key has a type... Hold jumps there, linear goes at a steady speed...'). The intent question 'is anything here meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?' comes only at the end, after the explanation and the candidate list.

Two candidates are named by layer and property, and both are framed as questions, not mistakes: Blink's Opacity ('Is it meant to snap on and off instead?') and Cut's Opacity ('Is that meant to be a sharp cut, or a short fade?'). Neither is called wrong, and there is no instruction to hold.

The record shows Easing as learned, which is the prerequisite this lesson builds on, but the mentor never mentions the learner's earlier easing work. It describes ease only generically ('ease speeds up and slows down naturally').
Every name and time matches the snapshot: Blink Opacity with 3 pairs starting at 1 s, Cut Opacity with 1 pair at 3 s, and Seal left out as a precomp.
